name: Agnes Osei
life: Agnes coaches children whose families assume rowing is too expensive. The first lesson is how to stand on a wet dock without looking as if you're scared. She admits to the children that sometimes she is scared too. Tuesday often includes a stop at the blocks below Foundry Lofts, where Agnes checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: My juniors need a place to learn how to step off a dock as much as they need water. I asked for Sunday mornings until the repair is finished. I'll sign for every scratch on the timber.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a dark green knitted vest and a pressed flower kept in the clear back of a phone case. Agnes has an aquiline nose and a square chin, with a blunt cut just below the ears. Agnes raises one eyebrow long before saying yes during a conversation.
personality: Agnes prefers exact instructions at work and pleasant surprises at home. The two standards occasionally collide, especially when a relative thinks dropping by counts as notice.
agenda: To give the juniors supervised time on the empty dock.
family: Alex Scott is Agnes’s cousin. Agnes offers the first invitation. Alex gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *Closing soup*, Alex says, “I put a rind in that was meant for my own dinner.”
connections: Rafe Costa. A coach asking to borrow the docks meets somebody who remembers when nobody needed to ask.

reactions.situation: A broker offers cash to keep the dock empty
reactions.response: Agnes finds out who was promised the empty dock time before discussing a price.
